title: Khalsa Authority Compared to Guru Nanak Establishing Angad

blocks.text: This page makes the transfer of authority visible through insignia and dress. The damaged lines describe the plume and garments being bestowed in a scene explicitly compared to Guru Nanak establishing Angad, so the Panth's honor is shown as a continuation of the Guru lineage rather than a break from it.

The page also stresses that the trust has been handed over to the Khalsa as a body. Counsel, prayer, companionship, and discipline are presented as the proper means by which that authority is exercised and preserved.

Its closing movement turns toward martyr resolve. The one who has received the Guru's charge must be ready to give his head without betraying the Panth, because delegated sovereignty is inseparable from sacrificial responsibility.
